html:
A huge round tomb that Augustus built for himself and his family in 28 BCE on the Campus Martius in Rome, by the Tiber.

He built it early in his rule, just after defeating Antony, who had asked to be buried in Alexandria. The tomb was a statement that Augustus's dynasty belonged to Rome. It was a ring of concrete walls some ninety metres across, topped with an earth mound planted with trees and a bronze statue of Augustus. By the entrance stood bronze pillars bearing his own account of his deeds, the Res Gestae.

The first to be buried there was his nephew Marcellus in 23 BCE. Agrippa, Augustus himself in 14 CE, Livia, Tiberius and other members of the family followed.

In later centuries it served as a fortress, a garden, a bullring and a concert hall. In the 1930s Mussolini cleared the buildings around it, and set the Ara Pacis beside it. After long restoration it reopened to visitors in 2021.
sum: A huge round tomb that Augustus built for himself and his family in 28 BCE on the Campus Martius in Rome, by the Tiber.
